title: Carlos Alcaraz Under Scrutiny as John McEnroe Makes Bold Claim About His 'Lucky' Escape at Australian Open - NewsBreak
text:
By Sreeja Banik ,
1 hours ago
Despite advancing to the third round of the 2026 Australian Open, Carlos Alcaraz has not received the usual praise from critics. John McEnroe, in particular, has scrutinized the Spaniard’s performance at the tournament.
Alcaraz’s best result at the Melbourne Major has been reaching the quarterfinals, which he achieved twice, in 2024 and 2025. Last year, he reached the final eight but was eliminated by Novak Djokovic, and the year before, he made it that far before falling to Alexander Zverev.
Carlos Alcaraz Has ‘Room for Improvement’ at Australian Open, Believes John McEnroe Alcaraz is the top seed at the 2026 Australian Open, and began his campaign by defeating Adam Walton 6-3, 7-6(2), 6-2 in the first round. He then faced Yannick Hanfmann in the second round, securing a 7-6(4), 6-3, 6-2 win.
However, Alcaraz’s victory over the German was not easy, as the first set lasted one hour and 18 minutes, marking the longest opening set of the Spaniard’s career at Grand Slams. He also faced break points during the match and encountered other challenges.
Recently, during an interview with TNT Sports, McEnroe pointed out that Alcaraz’s game wasn’t “clicking” against Hanfmann and that he was “lucky” to come away with the win.
“You know, he came out sort of, and wasn’t clicking, Alcaraz, and Hanfmann actually had, you know, early chances to get ahead and rattle Alcaraz. He did that a little bit in the first set, and honestly, Alcaraz was lucky to win that set in a way,” McEnroe said.
The former World No. 1 expressed that although Alcaraz didn’t play well initially, his performance improved as the match progressed. He mentioned that even after winning the second-round match at the Melbourne Major, Alcaraz still has “room for improvement.”
“He just didn’t really play that well, of course, the top guys want to save it for the second week. But you can’t bank on it. But he settled in as the match went on and started doing his thing a little better. But he’s not gonna look at this match and be like, ‘wow, okay, that’s where I need to be’, because he’s definitely got some room for improvement,” he added.
This year at the Australian Open, Alcaraz will be looking to complete a Career Grand Slam–an achievement that involves winning each of the four Major titles during a player’s career.
Who Will Carlos Alcaraz Face in the Third Round of the 2026 Australian Open? After his victory over Hanfmann in the second round of the 2026 Australian Open, Alcaraz is set to face Corentin Moutet in the third round of the tournament.
Moutet, seeded 32nd at the Melbourne Major, began his campaign by defeating Tristan Schoolkate with a scoreline of 6-4, 7-6(1), 6-3 in the first round. He then advanced to the third round when his second-round opponent, qualifier Michael Zheng, was forced to retire due to a left thigh injury with the score at 3-6, 6-1, 6-3, 2-0 (retd).
Alcaraz and Moutet have never faced each other on the ATP Tour, making their upcoming match at the 2026 Australian Open a first-time encounter. The winner of this match will progress to the fourth round, where they will meet either 14th seed Alejandro Davidovich Fokina or 19th seed Tommy Paul.
